description: Markdown formatting shorthand InputRules: bold, italic, inline code, and strikethrough convert live as the closing marker is typed.

tests.description: Typing '**foo**' in an empty paragraph converts to bold, no literal asterisks remain
Typing '*foo*' in an empty paragraph converts to italic, no literal asterisks remain
Typing '_foo_' converts to italic, same result as '*foo*'
Typing a backtick-delimited 'foo' in an empty paragraph converts to inline code, no literal backticks remain
Typing '~~foo~~' in an empty paragraph converts to strikethrough, no literal tildes remain
Typing '**foo**' straight through never transiently fires the italic rule before bold's closing '**' completes

Backspace immediately after a '**foo**' conversion reverts it via undoInputRule, restoring the literal typed text. The intermediate assertion (conversion happened before Backspace) is required, since a bare Backspace-is-a-no-op check would pass even without a conversion to revert.
Typing '**foo**bar' immediately continues -- the continuation text 'bar' is not bold (no stored-mark carry-over)

Inside an existing code mark, typing '**bold**', '*em*', and '~~strike~~' converts nothing -- markers stay literal inside the code span. Guards against the code-mark-suppression check being omitted or broken.
Typing exactly three backticks at the start of an empty paragraph still fires the existing codeBlockRule -- the new inline-code rule does not interfere.

Completing a bold conversion around a range that already contains a link preserves the link and its href -- only the delimiters are deleted, never the content. The link mark outranks strong in the schema, so the DOM serialization splits <strong> around the <a> rather than nesting it inside a single wrapper; both segments plus the link text are bold.

Typing '**bold *it* x**' straight through preserves the inner em mark created mid-type when bold's closing '**' completes (nested cross-delimiter emphasis). Em outranks strong in the schema, so the serialization nests <strong> inside <em> rather than the reverse.
Typing 'snake_case_name' does not italicize 'case' -- the underscore rule must not fire intraword, per CommonMark's flanking rule for '_' emphasis.

Typing 'a * b * c' (spaced asterisks, e.g. multiplication) does not italicize -- the em rule's flanking requirement (content must not start or end with whitespace) rejects delimiters with a space on the inner side.
Typing '**foo*' and stopping there (bold's second closing asterisk never arrives) leaves the text fully literal -- an odd, unmatched delimiter count must never convert.
